chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a right owed to him by another man and he has one witness.
He said: So he (the Imam) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to judge with one witness and the oath of the holder of the right, and that is in the matter of debt.

key_terms.الحق: Right, legal claim — here a financial entitlement or debt owed
key_terms.الدين: Debt, financial obligation — the specific domain to which this ruling applies
key_terms.شاهد واحد: Single witness — Islamic law normally requires two witnesses; this hadith establishes an exception for debt cases
key_terms.يمين: Oath (yamin) — the sworn testimony of the claimant supplementing the single witness

ai.seo_question: Can a judge in Islamic law rule on the basis of one witness and an oath?
ai.summary: Abu Basir asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about a judicial case where a claimant has only one witness to support his financial claim. The Imam responds by citing prophetic precedent: the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) used to render judgments in debt cases based on one witness combined with an oath from the claimant. This rule — known in Islamic jurisprudence as al-yamin ma'a al-shahid (oath with one witness) — is a recognized exception to the standard requirement of two male witnesses, and the Imam explicitly limits its scope to debt and financial claims (al-dayn), not to cases such as hudud or qisas.
